Coventry City manager Frank Lampard has revealed that Super Eagles midfielder Frank Onyeka has returned to training but remains a doubt for Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Crystal Palace at the CBS Arena.
The Nigerian international suffered an injury setback shortly before the November international break, ruling him out of Nigeria’s double-header against Tanzania in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.
Onyeka also missed Coventry City’s last two league fixtures against Sunderland and Everton, leaving Lampard without the midfielder during a crucial period of the campaign.
However, the 47-year-old has offered some encouragement ahead of the weekend encounter, confirming that the former Brentford player has resumed training with the squad.
Speaking during his pre-match press conference, Lampard remained cautious about the midfielder’s availability, suggesting that a final decision would depend on his fitness.
“He trained today so we’ll see,” the Coventry manager said when asked about Onyeka’s condition.

The midfielder’s return to training represents a positive development for Coventry, who will be keen to have his energy, physical presence and defensive qualities back in their midfield.
Onyeka initially joined the Sky Blues on loan from Brentford during the winter transfer window last season and quickly became an important figure in their push for promotion to the Premier League.
His contributions during the promotion campaign convinced the club to activate the purchase clause in his agreement, making his transfer permanent ahead of the current season.
The 28-year-old has since featured in eight matches across all competitions for Coventry, establishing himself as one of the options available to Lampard in midfield.
Lampard will be hoping to welcome Onyeka back into contention as Coventry prepare to face Crystal Palace following the international break.
The Sky Blues will be looking to rediscover their winning form after their recent league outings against Sunderland and Everton, with Saturday’s fixture presenting another opportunity to strengthen their position in the Premier League.
However, with Onyeka only just returning to training, the Coventry manager must decide whether the Nigerian is ready to feature or requires additional time to regain full match fitness.
His availability will be a welcome boost for Lampard, particularly as Coventry look to get their campaign back on track.
